**Five of the eight fiscal 2023 filings disclose a dollar total for leases entered into but not yet commenced at year-end.** All amounts below are in **millions of U.S. dollars**.

| Company | Fiscal 2023 year-end | Total for not-yet-commenced leases | Filing disclosure and source |
|---|---|---:|---|
| NVIDIA | January 29, 2023 | **$463 — operating leases** | Additional operating leases, primarily for data centers, expected to commence in fiscal 2024–2025. **Note 3, “Leases,” p. 67.** |
| Apple | September 30, 2023 | **$544** | “Future payments under additional leases” not yet commenced, primarily for corporate facilities and retail space. Apple does not split this total between operating and finance leases. **Note 8, “Leases,” p. 43 (PDF p. 46).** |
| JPMorgan Chase | December 31, 2023 | **$420 — operating leases** | “Additional future operating lease commitments” that “were signed but had not yet commenced.” **Note 18, “Leases—Firm as lessee,” p. 275 (PDF p. 277).** |
| ExxonMobil | December 31, 2023 | **$4,063 — operating leases; $2,256 — finance leases** | Explicitly states these separate totals as “undiscounted commitments for leases not yet commenced.” **Note 11, “Leases,” p. 98 (PDF p. 100).** |
| Boeing | December 31, 2023 | **$430** | Leases entered into but not yet commenced, primarily for a maintenance, repair and overhaul hangar supporting military aircraft programs. **Note 12, “Leases,” p. 79 (PDF p. 84).** |

**Berkshire Hathaway, Pfizer and Walmart do not state a separate dollar total for not-yet-commenced lessee leases in these filings.** Their lease-payment maturity totals are therefore not included above. Relevant lease disclosures are Berkshire’s Note 12, p. K-90; Pfizer’s Note 15, pp. 94–95; and Walmart’s Note 7, pp. 70–71.

The figures above are the disclosed totals for the uncommenced leases—not single-year payments, liabilities for commenced leases, or future receipts from leasing property to others.

**Four of the eight filings qualify: Walmart, Berkshire Hathaway, Pfizer and Boeing.**

| Filing | Named company acquired during fiscal 2025 | Supporting disclosure |
|---|---|---|
| **Walmart** | **VIZIO Holding Corp.** | States that Walmart U.S. “completed the acquisition” in **December 2024**, within Walmart’s fiscal year ended January 31, 2025. *2025 10-K, p. 34.* |
| **Berkshire Hathaway** | **Bell Laboratories, LLC** | Explicitly states: “Berkshire acquired Bell Laboratories, LLC … on **July 31, 2025**.” This is the Wisconsin-based rodent-control-products company. *2025 10-K, p. K-15 (PDF p. 17).* |
| **Pfizer** | **Metsera** | Note 2 states: “On **November 13, 2025**, we acquired Metsera,” and describes the per-share cash and contingent-value-right consideration. *2025 10-K, Note 2A, p. 64 (PDF p. 73).* |
| **Boeing** | **Spirit AeroSystems Holdings, Inc.** | Note 2 states that Boeing completed the acquisition on **December 8, 2025**, becoming the ultimate parent of Spirit and its subsidiaries. *2025 10-K, Note 2, p. 70 (PDF p. 74).* |

The other four do **not** meet the question’s filing-specific criteria:

- **NVIDIA:** Reports fiscal-2025 acquisitions and related goodwill, but does **not name the acquired companies**. Its named Arm transaction was terminated, not completed. *PDF pp. 34, 62, 65.*
- **Apple:** Does not report a completed fiscal-2025 acquisition of a **named entire company**.
- **JPMorgan Chase:** Its business-combination disclosures concern earlier acquisitions. The 2025 First Republic settlement was not a new acquisition; the underlying transaction occurred in **2023** and involved certain assets and liabilities. *Note 34, PDF p. 314; Note 15, PDF p. 274.*
- **ExxonMobil:** The 2025 Superior Graphite transaction involved **“key technology and assets,”** not the entire company. Pioneer and Denbury closed in **2024** and **2023**, respectively. *PDF pp. 56, 114–115.*

Berkshire’s **OxyChem** acquisition is also excluded: it closed on **January 2, 2026**, after its 2025 fiscal year ended. *Note 2, PDF p. 80.*

**Three of the eight fiscal 2025 Form 10-Ks disclose the requested year-end balance: Walmart, Pfizer and Boeing.** All amounts below are in **millions of U.S. dollars**.

| Company | Fiscal 2025 year-end | Year-end balance | Filing disclosure |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **Walmart** | January 31, 2025 | **$5,725** | “Confirmed obligations outstanding at the end of the year,” in Note 1, **Supplier Financing Program Obligations** (p. 61). |
| **Pfizer** | December 31, 2025 | **$574** | “Confirmed obligations outstanding, ending,” in Note 8C, **Supplier Finance Program Obligation** (printed pp. 82–83; PDF pp. 92–93). |
| **Boeing** | December 31, 2025 | **$1,994** | “Ending balance – December 31” of accounts payable to suppliers participating in supply chain financing programs, in Note 15, **Supply Chain Financing Programs** (printed p. 90; PDF p. 94). |

**NVIDIA, Apple, JPMorgan Chase, Berkshire Hathaway and ExxonMobil do not disclose a fiscal 2025 year-end supplier-finance obligation balance in the specified filings.** That is a lack of a disclosed balance—not a reported balance of zero.

The figures above are the **closing balances**, not annual additions, invoices confirmed or paid, changes during the year, or prior-year balances.

**Only NVIDIA and Pfizer disclose qualifying dollar amounts** in the specified fiscal 2022 Forms 10-K.

| Company | Amount of earnings intended to remain indefinitely reinvested overseas | Filing evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| **NVIDIA** | **Approximately $1.05 billion in Israel; $232 million in the United Kingdom** | “As of January 30, 2022, we intend to indefinitely reinvest approximately $1.05 billion and $232 million of cumulative undistributed earnings” held by certain subsidiaries in those countries, respectively. **Note 14—Income Taxes, p. 75.** |
| **Pfizer** | **$60.0 billion** | As of December 31, 2022, Pfizer had not made a U.S. tax provision on “$60.0 billion of unremitted earnings of our international subsidiaries,” and states that “these earnings are intended to be indefinitely reinvested overseas.” **Note 5C—Deferred Taxes, printed p. 70 (PDF p. 77).** |

The other six filings **do not state an amount of earnings meeting your criteria**:

- **Apple:** No qualifying accumulated, indefinitely reinvested earnings amount is disclosed. Its foreign pretax earnings and deemed-repatriation tax payable are different measures. **Note 5—Income Taxes, printed pp. 41–43; Liquidity and Capital Resources, printed p. 25.**
- **JPMorgan Chase:** No qualifying amount is disclosed in **Note 25—Income Taxes, printed pp. 270–272**.
- **Berkshire Hathaway:** Says accumulated undistributed earnings of certain foreign subsidiaries are expected to be reinvested indefinitely, but gives **no dollar amount of those earnings**. **Note 19—Income Taxes, p. K-102 (PDF p. 104).**
- **ExxonMobil:** Says undistributed foreign-subsidiary earnings are expected to be indefinitely reinvested, but gives **no dollar amount of those earnings**. **Note 19—Income Taxes, printed p. 116 (PDF p. 118).**
- **Walmart:** Its approximately **$3 billion** figure is **unrecorded deferred tax liabilities** associated with indefinitely reinvested unremitted earnings—not the earnings themselves—so it does not count. **Note 9—Taxes, “Unremitted Earnings,” p. 73.**
- **Boeing:** Says certain non-U.S. subsidiaries’ undistributed earnings are indefinitely reinvested, but gives **no dollar amount of those earnings**. **Note 4—Income Taxes, printed p. 75 (PDF p. 79).**

**Three of the eight filings qualify: NVIDIA, Apple and JPMorgan Chase.** Their Item 9B disclosures name the following distinct directors or officers as adopting qualifying plans during the last fiscal quarter:

| Filing | Number of people | People named and adoption dates | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **NVIDIA fiscal 2024 10-K** — year ended January 28, 2024 | **1** | **John O. Dabiri**, director — December 18, 2023 | Item 9B, p. 45 |
| **Apple fiscal 2024 10-K** — year ended September 28, 2024 | **2** | **Deirdre O’Brien**, SVP, Retail — August 27, 2024; **Jeff Williams**, COO — August 29, 2024 | Item 9B, printed p. 52 (PDF p. 55) |
| **JPMorgan Chase 2024 10-K** — year ended December 31, 2024 | **5** | **Lori Beer** — November 15; **James Dimon** — November 7; **Robin Leopold** — November 4; **Jennifer Piepszak** — October 30; **Troy Rohrbaugh** — November 15, all in 2024 | Item 9B, printed p. 41 (PDF p. 43) |

Each of these disclosures expressly states that the arrangements were intended to satisfy the affirmative defense of Rule 10b5-1(c).

**The other five filings do not qualify:** each expressly reports no director/officer adoptions of the covered arrangements during its final fiscal quarter.

| Filing | Source for the negative disclosure |
|---|---|
| Walmart fiscal 2024 | Item 9B, p. 81 |
| Berkshire Hathaway 2024 | Item 9B, printed p. K-117 (PDF p. 119) |
| Pfizer 2024 | Item 9B, printed p. 109 (PDF p. 121) |
| ExxonMobil 2024 | Item 9B, printed p. 29 (PDF p. 31) |
| Boeing 2024 | Item 9B, printed p. 127 (PDF p. 131) |

These counts are of **different people, not plans**, and exclude company share-repurchase arrangements.

**Two of the eight filings report qualifying preferred-stock issuances during fiscal 2024: JPMorgan Chase and Boeing.**

| Filing | Issuance date | What was issued |
|---|---|---|
| **JPMorgan Chase — 2024 Form 10-K** | **March 12, 2024** | **$2.5 billion of fixed-rate reset non-cumulative preferred stock, Series NN**, represented by depositary shares. Note 21 expressly gives the issuance date. See printed pp. **291–292** (PDF pp. 293–294). |
| **Boeing — 2024 Form 10-K** | **October 31, 2024** | **115 million depositary shares**, representing **5.75 million shares of 6.00% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock**. See Note 19, “Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock,” printed p. **106** (PDF p. 110). |

The specified fiscal-2024 filings for **NVIDIA, Apple, Walmart, Berkshire Hathaway, Pfizer and ExxonMobil do not report an issuance of their own preferred stock during those fiscal years**.

Two date distinctions matter: JPMorgan’s filing also reports a **February 4, 2025** Series OO issuance, which falls outside fiscal 2024; Boeing’s **October 30, 2024** issuance was common stock—the preferred-stock issuance occurred the following day.

**Only ExxonMobil and Boeing** disclose a fiscal-2022 year-end recorded liability balance that meets your definition.

| Company | Recorded liability at fiscal year-end 2022 (USD millions) | Filing support |
|---|---:|---|
| **ExxonMobil** | **730** | Under “Environmental Liabilities,” the filing covers remediation obligations for assets or businesses currently owned or previously disposed of, and states that “the balance sheet reflects liabilities of $730 million as of December 31, 2022.” *XOM_2022_10K.pdf*, printed p. 68 (PDF p. 70). |
| **Boeing** | **752** | Note 13’s environmental-remediation rollforward reports an “Ending balance – December 31” of **$752 million** for 2022. The accompanying text identifies this as estimated costs to remediate sites, including long-term operation and maintenance. *BA_2022_10K.pdf*, printed pp. 83–84 (PDF pp. 87–88). |

The other six filings—**NVIDIA, Apple, JPMorgan Chase, Berkshire Hathaway, Pfizer and Walmart—do not state a qualifying dollar balance**. That does **not** mean their liability was zero.

In particular:
- **Pfizer** says it accrued estimated remediation costs for the former Wyeth/American Cyanamid Bound Brook site, but does not give the balance. Its **$88 million** and **$148 million** environmental figures are annual expenditures, not the liability. *PFE_2022_10K.pdf*, printed pp. 12 and 95.
- **Berkshire Hathaway’s** asbestos, environmental and latent-injury claim reserves concern insurance/reinsurance obligations, not cleanup of its own operating sites, so they are excluded.
- **Boeing’s $1,058 million** is the amount by which the high end of possible remediation costs exceeded its recorded liability—not the liability itself.

**Two of the six FY2021 filings state the requested subsidiary dividend capacity: JPMorgan Chase and Berkshire Hathaway.**

| Company | Capacity (US$ billions) | What the filing states |
|---|---:|---|
| **JPMorgan Chase** | **Approximately 20** | At **January 1, 2022**, its banking subsidiaries could pay, in aggregate, approximately $20 billion in dividends to their respective bank holding companies **without prior approval of their relevant banking regulators**. Capacity in 2022 would be supplemented by earnings during the year. *2021 Form 10-K, Note 26, printed p. 280 (PDF p. 282).* |
| **Berkshire Hathaway** | **Approximately 30** | Its principal insurance subsidiaries could declare up to approximately $30 billion in **ordinary dividends during 2022 without prior regulatory approval**. *2021 Form 10-K, Note 15, “Dividend restrictions—Insurance subsidiaries,” printed p. K-90 (PDF p. 92).* |

**Apple, Pfizer, ExxonMobil and Boeing do not state a dollar amount meeting that criterion in their FY2021 filings.** This means no qualifying amount is disclosed—not that their subsidiary dividend capacity was zero.

**Only Pfizer and Walmart** disclose a company-wide fiscal 2023 dollar amount explicitly labeled advertising expense or advertising costs.

| Company | Fiscal 2023 amount (US$ billions) | Filing evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| **Pfizer** | **Approximately 3.7** | “Advertising expenses totaled approximately $3.7 billion in 2023.” — *2023 Form 10-K*, Note 1J, printed p. 61 (PDF p. 70). |
| **Walmart** | **4.1** | “Advertising costs were $4.1 billion, $3.9 billion and $3.2 billion for fiscal 2023, 2022 and 2021, respectively.” — *2023 Form 10-K*, Note 1, “Advertising Costs,” p. 64. |

**The other six filings—NVIDIA, Apple, JPMorgan Chase, Berkshire Hathaway, ExxonMobil and Boeing—do not disclose a qualifying amount.** In particular:

- **JPMorgan Chase’s $4.591 billion is labeled “Marketing,”** so it does not count.
- **Berkshire Hathaway’s discussion of reduced GEICO advertising expenses** is not a company-wide total advertising-expense amount, so it does not count.

“No qualifying amount” means no disclosure meeting your definition—not zero advertising spending.

**Three of the eight FY2022 filings state a qualifying Moody’s long-term rating: JPMorgan Chase, Pfizer and Walmart.**

| Company | Moody’s long-term rating stated | Latest reported basis and source |
|---|---|---|
| **JPMorgan Chase & Co.** | **A1** | The credit-ratings table as of **December 31, 2022** gives **A1** for the parent company’s “long-term issuer” rating. The filing also says Moody’s upgraded it from A2 on September 29, 2022. This is distinct from the subsidiaries’ ratings. *2022 Form 10-K, “Credit ratings,” printed p. 104 (PDF p. 106).* |
| **Pfizer Inc.** | **A1** | The table of **current ratings** gives **A1** for Pfizer’s senior unsecured long-term debt. The accompanying text says Moody’s raised the rating from A2 in **November 2022**. *2022 Form 10-K, “Credit Ratings,” printed p. 43 (PDF p. 50).* |
| **Walmart Inc.** | **Aa2** | The table of ratings as of **January 31, 2022** gives **Aa2** for Walmart’s long-term debt under “Moody’s Investors Service.” *FY2022 Form 10-K, “Capital Resources,” pp. 44–45.* |

The FY2022 filings for **NVIDIA, Apple, Berkshire Hathaway, ExxonMobil and Boeing do not state a Moody’s long-term rating meeting your criterion**. That is a finding about disclosure in these filings—not a claim that those companies lacked Moody’s ratings.

**Three of the eight filings identify a collective chief operating decision maker (CODM): JPMorgan Chase, Berkshire Hathaway and ExxonMobil.**

| Filing | Group identified as the CODM | Filing language and source |
|---|---|---|
| **JPMorgan Chase — 2024 Form 10-K** | **Operating Committee** | Says the committee’s members “act collectively as the Firm’s chief operating decision maker.” *Business Segment & Corporate Results*, p. 70 (PDF p. 72). |
| **Berkshire Hathaway — 2024 Form 10-K** | **An unnamed group comprising the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, the Vice Chairman of Insurance Operations, and the Vice Chairman of Non-Insurance Operations** | Says its CODM “consists of” those three positions and that “[t]his group” is ultimately responsible for significant capital-allocation decisions and evaluating operating performance. Note 26, *Business segment data*, p. K-108 (PDF p. 110). |
| **ExxonMobil — 2024 Form 10-K** | **Management Committee (MC)** | Explicitly says the MC is considered “collectively, and not in their individual capacity” to be the CODM. It includes the CEO, CFO and two Senior Vice Presidents serving as contact executives overseeing the Upstream and Product Solutions businesses. Note 18, *Disclosures about Segments and Related Information*, p. 108 (PDF p. 110). |

The other five specified filings—NVIDIA, Apple, Walmart, Pfizer and Boeing—do **not** identify a collective executive group as their CODM.
